messages:
maya: Drafting an RFC + short PRD for runtime prioritization heuristics and launch criteria. TL;DR: weighted routing by latency budget, model-cost tiers, per-prefix KV TTLs and evict heuristics. Seeking acceptance criteria and edge-case calls. Link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/runtime-priority-draft :eyes:

jon: skimmed it. big Q: how do dedicated customers pin a model/version? this changes routing semantics. need a clear override path in the PRD.

maya: good call. PRD has a 'customer pinning' section but it's terse. proposal: pinning wins always, but we still surface cost/latency signals. would that be acceptable?

lee: +1 for pin wins. also propose we scope rollout: hosted first, then Dedicated with opt-in flag. don't try to bend private/VPC for the first launch. keeps config surface small.

sasha: edge-case: very long-context chats where KV warming is expensive. if TTL eviction is too aggressive we pay warm cost, if too lax we blow memory. need an acceptance test for 'steady-state token cost within X% of baseline' and a fallback to smaller model on mem pressure.

samir: suggested acceptance criteria in comments: 1) 95p latency <= baseline + 10ms for 90% of routes; 2) median unit token cost reduced by >= 8% for qualifying workloads; 3) no functional regressions on conversational eval sets. put numbers in PRD.

maya: adding samir numbers. also adding rollout gates: feature flag, canary 5% traffic for 48h, health metrics stable (error rate, p95, cost).

lee: regarding health metrics, we need explicit thresholds for autoscale/backoff. e.g., if p95 exceeds gate by 20% for 10m -> auto-fallback to model-variant C and rollback canary. add that as an operational acceptance criteria.

sasha: another edge case: model-variant mismatches (quantized variant missing kernel). config snippet suggestion: 
```
routing: 
  - name: latency_budget_routing
    budgets: [50, 150] # ms
    fallback_order: [base, quantized, small]
    kv_ttl_policy: per_prefix_adaptive
```
We should include how we map budgets to kernels.

maya: love the snippet. I'll add explicit mapping table to RFC (budget -> kernel selection -> fallback). also will include per-prefix heuristics: hot prefixes keep longer TTL, ephemeral ones evict quickly (configurable thresholds).

infra-bot: FYI: infra constraints - some older GPU hosts don't support the new quant kernels. add capability discovery step to the deploy checklist.

deploy-bot: canary started at 1801236810 for 5% traffic. monitoring links: https://dashboards/redwood/runtime/priorities-canary

jon: quick ask from product: customers X and Y asked for a 'latency-first' toggle. should we bake that in or expose a visibility flag only?

maya: propose visibility flag now + plan for toggle in v2 if customers escalate. keeps scope smaller for launch. calling for final reviews by EOD tomorrow. please add short comments inline on the doc. :pray:
